subject.title: Session `status` field values ("failed", "timeout", "done") mislead agents into spawning duplicate sessions

question: Should OpenClaw solve this by adding a backward-compatible `resumable` signal and model guidance, by renaming shipped status values, or by scoping the hint only to the agent-facing session tools?
rationale: The remaining fix changes a shared session-state contract used by Gateway/UI/tool consumers, so automation should not choose status naming, `killed` semantics, or shared-row scope without maintainer intent.

options.title: Add backward-compatible resumability metadata
options.body: Add a `resumable` or equivalent explicit signal plus model-facing guidance while preserving existing status values for compatibility.

options.title: Rename status values
options.body: Treat the current names as too misleading and accept a breaking or migrated status contract across Gateway and tool consumers.

options.title: Limit the hint to agent tools
options.body: Keep Gateway rows unchanged and teach only the model-facing `sessions_list` projection how to communicate resumability.

recommendation.title: Add backward-compatible resumability metadata
recommendation.body: Add a `resumable` or equivalent explicit signal plus model-facing guidance while preserving existing status values for compatibility.

likelyOwner.reason: tyler6204 authored the merged status/timing surface and merged the broad session-management PR that owns this user-visible contract.
